players.product: power transformers and grid equipment buyer — US utility (largest HD Hyundai Electric customer)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results: CEO said full-year adjusted earnings per share of $3.71 were up over 8% from 2024, slightly better than the top end of the range communicated at the December investor conference. CFO: FPL's full-year earnings per share increased $0.21, driven by regulatory capital employed growth of approximately 8.1%; FPL's retail sales increased 1.7% on a weather-normalized basis as it added over 90,000 customers. Energy Resources reported full-year adjusted earnings growth of approximately 13%: contributions from new investments up $0.47 per share, existing clean energy assets down $0.04 per share, customer supply and trading up $0.04 per share, and other impacts down $0.30 per share (including higher financing costs of $0.17 per share). Corporate and Other decreased by $0.12 per share on higher interest costs. Outlook as of this call: 2026 adjusted EPS range of $3.92 to $4.02 unchanged, targeting the high end; dividends per share to grow roughly 10% per year through 2026 off a 2024 base and 6% per year from year-end 2026 through 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 adjusted EPS $3.71 (up over 8%); FPL EPS increased $0.21; regulatory capital employed growth approximately 8.1%; Energy Resources adjusted earnings growth approximately 13%; new investments +$0.47 per share; dividend growth roughly 10% per year through 2026, 6% per year through 2028

quarterly_data.signal: FPL enters 2026 with a new four-year rate agreement running through the remainder of the decade (the Florida Public Service Commission approved it unanimously in November and issued its final order the week before the call): allowed midpoint regulatory ROE of 10.95% (range 9.95% to 11.95%), equity ratio 59%, a rate stabilization mechanism (aggregate after-tax balance of approximately $1.5 billion over the term), and a large load tariff that the CEO said gives hyperscalers speed to market at a competitive price while protecting existing customers from bearing the infrastructure build-out costs needed to support hyperscalers. FPL capital expenditures were approximately $2.1 billion in Q4, bringing full-year 2025 capital investments to roughly $8.9 billion; FPL expects to invest between $90 billion and $100 billion through 2032. FPL expects typical residential bills to rise only about 2% annually between 2025 and 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: FPL Q4 capex approximately $2.1 billion; 2025 FPL capex roughly $8.9 billion; allowed midpoint ROE 10.95% (9.95% to 11.95%); equity ratio 59%; approximately $1.5 billion rate stabilization balance

quarterly_data.signal: FPL large load (point in time): CEO said FPL's speed to market and service have created large load interest of over 20 gigawatts to date, with advanced discussions on about nine gigawatts, a portion of which FPL now believes it could begin serving as soon as 2028; every gigawatt is equivalent to roughly $2 billion of CapEx and earns the same return on equity as other FPL investments. FPL CEO Armando Pimentel expects announcements regarding large load in FPL's service territory in 2026. Management said customers want certainty before "plopping down the $10 billion or so" of capital for one of these data centers, and are waiting on data center legislation in Tallahassee (e.g., water usage), where management expects a constructive outcome; FPL President Scott Borys said the Senate bill largely pushes for protections FPL's tariff already provides.
quarterly_data.figure: over 20 gigawatts of large load interest; about nine gigawatts in advanced discussions; first service as soon as 2028; roughly $2 billion of CapEx per gigawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Energy Resources had its best origination year for the fourth year in a row, adding nearly 13.5 gigawatts of new generation and battery storage projects to backlog in 2025, including a record quarter of approximately 3.6 gigawatts since the Q3 call; 1.7 gigawatts, almost 50% of Q4 additions, were solar. Backlog stands at approximately 30 gigawatts after roughly 3.6 gigawatts of projects placed into service since the Q3 call; approximately 35 gigawatts originated over the last three years. CFO: 2025 origination reflects growing demand, "including from hyperscalers that are looking for speed-to-market power solutions." Energy Resources put 7.2 gigawatts into commercial operation (a single-year record), and FPL plus Energy Resources placed approximately 8.7 gigawatts of new generation and storage in service in 2025. Development expectations through 2032 assume market share of about 15% to 20% in renewables, 20% to 30% in storage and 5% to 10% in gas; CEO expects the mix to keep trending toward solar, storage and ultimately gas relative to wind.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 13.5 gigawatts added to backlog in 2025; approximately 3.6 gigawatts in Q4 (record quarter); backlog approximately 30 gigawatts; 7.2 gigawatts placed in commercial operation; approximately 8.7 gigawatts placed in service company-wide

quarterly_data.signal: Battery storage (point in time): CEO said storage now represents almost one-third of the 30-gigawatt backlog, with nearly five gigawatts originated over the past twelve months, and that "battery storage is the only new capacity resource available at scale." Energy Resources placed over two gigawatts of battery storage into service in 2025, increasing its annual battery storage build from 2024 by roughly 220%. The stand-alone and co-located battery storage pipeline totals 95 gigawatts; co-locating storage at sites that already have grid connections can effectively double capacity at a site, expanding each site could potentially double total backlog, and long-duration opportunities are at an early stage. A domestic battery supply is secured through 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: 95-gigawatt stand-alone and co-located storage pipeline; storage almost one-third of the 30-gigawatt backlog; over two gigawatts of storage placed in service in 2025 (up roughly 220%)

quarterly_data.signal: Gas-fired generation and equipment supply (point in time): the potential gas-fired generation pipeline has topped 20 gigawatts, and NextEra has secured gas turbine slots with GE Vernova to support four gigawatts of gas-fired generation projects, which the CEO said would be put mainly against the data center hub opportunities, with more secured as those discussions advance. CEO: "given the relationship and partnership that we have with GE Vernova, our hands on gas turbines at an economic and competitive price is not the top of my list of things to be concerned about"; no specific pricing terms were given, and pricing remains consistent with what was shared in December. Development expectations assume six gigawatts (the midpoint) of new gas-fired generation build through 2032. Solar panels are secured to meet development expectations through 2029 with construction begun on those projects, and permitted project inventory covers 1.5 times the forecast.
quarterly_data.figure: gas pipeline topped 20 gigawatts; GE Vernova turbine slots for four gigawatts; six gigawatts of new gas build (midpoint) through 2032; 1.5 times project inventory coverage

quarterly_data.signal: Data center hub strategy (point in time): 20 potential hubs under discussion with the market, expected to rise to 40 by year-end, under the '15 by 35' origination channel whose goal is for Energy Resources to place in service 15 gigawatts of new generation for data center hubs by 2035; the CEO said he would be disappointed not to double the goal and deliver at least 30 gigawatts through the channel by 2035. The 15 gigawatts is roughly six gigawatts of gas-fired generation (the CEO clarified: by 2032) with renewables and storage for the balance. Energy Resources is positioning for bring your own generation (BYOG), where hyperscalers bring and pay for their own power generation infrastructure, using its renewables and storage portfolio as a speed-to-market 'hook' for a data center's initial phase before adding capacity through new gas-fired generation or SMRs. The CEO said larger deals will be announced as they happen rather than held for quarterly calls.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 hubs, rising to 40 by year-end; 15 gigawatts by 2035 goal, at least 30 gigawatts hoped; roughly six gigawatts of gas in the mix

quarterly_data.signal: Nuclear: the Duane Arnold recommissioning in Iowa continues, made possible by the twenty-five-year power purchase agreement with Google announced last year. NextEra has six gigawatts of SMR co-location opportunities at its nuclear sites and is working to develop new greenfield sites; it narrowed the 96 or so SMR OEMs to about 12 for deep dives, has a development team focused 100% on SMRs, historically prefers competition among suppliers over locking in one counterparty, and requires risk sharing that caps its financial exposure (a four-party structure with the OEM, the hyperscaler and the government). CFO: SMRs are not in the base plan and would be upside. Point Beach (Wisconsin) received a subsequent license renewal for another twenty years and signed a PPA extension for 14% of the plant's capacity, contributing $0.03 of annual adjusted EPS (CEO: extrapolated to the rest of the plant, $0.21); Seabrook (New Hampshire) is seeing similar interest, with 1.7 gigawatts of capacity offered to the market between the two plants. Renewables recontracting opportunities total up to six gigawatts through 2032.
quarterly_data.figure: six gigawatts of SMR co-location opportunities; 96 or so SMR OEMs narrowed to about 12; Point Beach PPA extension for 14% of capacity = $0.03 annual adjusted EPS ($0.21 if extrapolated); 1.7 gigawatts of nuclear capacity offered to market

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission and gas infrastructure: NextEra Energy Transmission has $8 billion of total regulated and secured capital and has secured roughly $5 billion in new projects since 2023, including PJM's December recommendation that NextEra Energy Transmission and Exelon be selected to develop a new $1.7 billion high-voltage transmission line expected to enhance the flow of more than seven gigawatts of power across the region (PJM decision expected the month after the call; asked by an analyst about pushback in Pennsylvania, the CFO said confidence "continues to be high" and that PJM continues to support the project). Energy Resources holds ownership interests in more than 1,000 miles of FERC-regulated pipelines and acquired a portion of ConEd's interest in Mountain Valley Pipeline in January; on January 9 it closed the acquisition of natural gas supplier Symmetry Energy Solutions, which operates in 34 states. The combined electric and gas transmission business is expected to reach $20 billion of regulated and invested capital by 2032, a 20% CAGR off a 2025 base. Management put the 2026 reduction in gas infrastructure adjusted EBITDA at "$50 million or so".
quarterly_data.figure: $1.7 billion PJM transmission line (with Exelon); $8 billion regulated and secured capital; roughly $5 billion secured since 2023; more than 1,000 miles of FERC-regulated pipelines
